country.name: Morocco
country.summary: Morocco is Africa's leading container gateway: Tanger Med handled 11.1m TEU and 161m tonnes in 2025 (up 8.4% and 13.3%), anchoring a 3,000 ha industrial platform of 1,500+ companies. The national system is run by two authorities (ANP for the commercial ports incl. Casablanca, Jorf Lasfar, Agadir, Safi, Mohammedia; Tanger Med Port Authority for Tanger Med) with Marsa Maroc (listed, 67m tonnes and 3m+ TEU in 2025) as the dominant domestic terminal operator alongside APM Terminals, Eurogate/Contship, Hapag-Lloyd, MSC/TIL and CMA CGM. Headline projects are Nador West Med (first commercial calls Q4 2026; ~5m TEU and 35m t at full build), Dakhla Atlantique (MAD 12-15bn, ~62-65% built mid-2026, opening 2028-29) and Marsa Maroc's MAD 21bn 2025-2030 expansion plan, backed by a MAD 96bn rail programme (Kenitra-Marrakech LGV, Nador West Med link). DP World has no terminal concession in Morocco; the competitive landscape is APM Terminals, Eurogate, MSC/TIL, CMA CGM and Marsa Maroc.

ports.name: Tanger Med
ports.operator: Tanger Med Port Authority (TMPA, Tanger Med Group); container terminals: TC1 APM Terminals Tangier, TC2 Eurogate Tanger, TC3 Tanger Alliance (Marsa Maroc with Hapag-Lloyd, Eurogate/Contship), TC4 APM Terminals MedPort Tangier; Marsa Maroc general-cargo terminal
ports.concession: Four container terminals under long-term concessions from TMPA: TC1 APM Terminals (since 2007), TC2 Eurogate (since 2008), TC4 APM Terminals MedPort Tangier (since 2019), TC3 Tanger Alliance (since 2021); terms n/a
ports.capacity: 9m TEU/year across 4 container terminals (TC1 1.5m/800 m, TC2 1.5m/800 m, TC3 1.5m/800 m, TC4 5m/2,000 m); hydrocarbon terminal 500,000 t storage; passenger/ro-ro port with 8 berths; 2 car terminals (20 ha)
ports.throughput: 11,106,164 TEU (2025, +8.4%); 161m tonnes; 535,203 TIR trucks; 526,862 vehicles; 3.22m passengers; 8.64m t hydrocarbons; 16,686 ship calls (2025)
ports.projects: TC4 latest extension commissioned 2025; APM Terminals announced a 2m TEU expansion of MedPort Tangier (Dec 2024) taking the terminal well beyond nominal capacity; port already operating above 9m TEU nominal capacity
ports.notes: Africa's and the Mediterranean's largest container port; transhipment-dominated with strong gateway traffic from the Tangier automotive cluster (Renault, Stellantis supply chain). Rail freight link to the ONCF network and A4/A1 motorways to Casablanca. Competitor concessions: APM Terminals (Maersk), Eurogate/Contship, Hapag-Lloyd, Marsa Maroc. No DP World presence.

ports.name: Port of Casablanca
ports.operator: ANP (port authority); Marsa Maroc operates the East container terminal, ro-ro, multipurpose and minerals terminals, plus the TC3PC container terminal via subsidiary; Somaport (CMA CGM) operates a second container terminal
ports.concession: Marsa Maroc terminals under ANP concessions (Marsa Maroc created 2006 from ODEP); TC3PC concession to Marsa Maroc subsidiary; Somaport concession to CMA CGM group; terms n/a
ports.capacity: Marsa Maroc: 700,000 TEU domestic capacity, 1.3m TEU incl. TC3PC; container quay 600 m, draft 12 m, ~60 ha yard; general cargo 1,545 m of quay (12 berths); ro-ro 5,000-vehicle multi-storey park; multipurpose terminal deepened to -12 m (2026)
ports.throughput: c. 21.3m tonnes/year, ~38% of national (non-Tanger Med) traffic; Marsa Maroc terminals ~10m t/year and ~800,000 TEU incl. TC3PC (2019, latest published breakdown); Marsa Maroc group 3m+ TEU (2025)
ports.projects: Marsa Maroc MAD 475m deepening/upgrade of the multipurpose terminal (230 m of -12 m quay commissioned April 2026, 530 m by 2028, >8m t/year capacity, vessels up to 60,000 dwt); container capacity expansion toward 2m TEU (~US$320m) within Marsa Maroc's MAD 21bn 2025-2030 plan; ANP/government ~US$300m Casablanca port expansion (2026); cruise terminal (450,000 pax) opened 2022
ports.notes: Main import/export gateway for the Casablanca-Settat industrial hinterland; land-constrained urban port. Competitor concessions: Marsa Maroc, CMA CGM (Somaport). Rail-connected (ONCF) and on the A1/A3/A7 motorway hub.

ports.name: Nador West Med
ports.operator: Nador West Med SA (state port company); East terminal (WMCT) JV Marsa Maroc 50%+1 / Terminal Investment Ltd (MSC) 50%-1; West terminal JV Marsa Maroc 51% / CMA Terminals 49%
ports.concession: East container terminal: Marsa Maroc–TIL/MSC JV finalised Jan 2026; West container terminal: Marsa Maroc–CMA CGM agreement (2025), progressively operational from 2027; terms n/a
ports.capacity: East terminal 3.4m TEU, 1,520 m quay, 18 m draft, ~70 ha yard; West terminal 1.8m TEU, 900 m quay, 18 m draft, 60 ha, 8 STS cranes; full complex ~5m TEU and 35m t bulk; 5.4 km breakwaters, 4 km of quay; hydrocarbons and Morocco's first LNG (FSU) terminal planned
ports.projects: Combined public/private investment cited at MAD 51bn (~US$5.1bn) incl. >EUR 300m European financing; 800 ha industrial zone (expandable to 5,000 ha); Selouane–NWM rail link (52 km) and Guercif–Nador motorway (104 km, MAD 5.5bn, 2028) as hinterland links; operational trials completed Sept 2026
ports.notes: Second Mediterranean transhipment hub after Tanger Med, aimed at eastern Med/Algeria-adjacent and Oriental-region cargo. Competitor concessions: MSC/TIL and CMA CGM with Marsa Maroc. No DP World role.

ports.name: Jorf Lasfar
ports.operator: ANP (authority); OCP Group (phosphate/phosphoric acid and fertiliser terminals); Marsa Maroc (multipurpose/bulk terminal); Taqa Morocco coal import terminal
ports.concession: OCP and Marsa Maroc operate under ANP concessions; terms n/a
ports.capacity: Morocco's main mineral/industrial bulk port serving the OCP Jorf Lasfar platform (world's largest phosphoric acid complex) and the Jorf Lasfar coal power station
ports.throughput: n/a (ANP does not publish a recent figure in sources consulted)
ports.projects: 'Green Basin' expansion led by ANP: >3,500 linear m of new quays, >1,000 m of breakwater and deepening of 1,000 m of existing quay to serve battery-materials and green-fuel exports (Cobco NMC precursors, Fluoralpha, Falcon Energy graphite, Tinci electrolytes); geotechnical studies under way (2026). OCP's PMP fifth phosphoric acid line inaugurated 2026
ports.notes: Strategic for OCP export logistics; hinterland battery gigafactory cluster (Jorf Lasfar/El Jadida) creates new container and project-cargo demand. Competitor concession: Marsa Maroc.

ports.name: Port of Agadir
ports.operator: ANP (authority); Marsa Maroc (2 terminals incl. container/bulk West quay); SMA (Marsa Maroc subsidiary) at North quay terminal
ports.concession: Marsa Maroc / SMA under ANP concessions; terms n/a
ports.capacity: Container capacity >150,000 TEU/year; West quay 670 m, draft 10.5 m; oil quay draft 8.5 m; reefer plugs for 900 containers
ports.throughput: c. 3m tonnes/year (Marsa Maroc terminals, latest published)
ports.projects: Included in Marsa Maroc's MAD 21bn 2025-2030 investment programme; details n/a
ports.notes: Cold-chain gateway for Souss-Massa citrus, vegetables and fish exports; hinterland zones Haliopolis/Agropole. Competitor concession: Marsa Maroc.

ports.name: Port of Mohammedia
ports.operator: ANP (authority); Marsa Maroc (oil terminal stations A/B and inner-port terminal)
ports.concession: Marsa Maroc under ANP concession; terms n/a
ports.capacity: Oil terminal capacity >20m t/year, 580 m quay, draft 17 m; inner port 330 m quay, draft 6-6.7 m; 47,000 m2 yards
ports.throughput: c. 5m tonnes/year (crude, refined products, LPG, chemicals)
ports.projects: ANP has studied siting Morocco's first LNG import terminal at Mohammedia (not confirmed; Nador West Med FSU now favoured)
ports.notes: Morocco's main hydrocarbon import port, historically linked to the idle SAMIR refinery (in liquidation since 2015-16). Competitor concession: Marsa Maroc.

ports.name: New Port of Safi (Safi Atlantique)
ports.operator: ANP (authority); OCP Group (phosphate export terminal, ZPMC-equipped); Safi Energy coal power plant import terminal
ports.concession: OCP phosphate terminal (ZPMC equipment contract MAD 2bn); terms n/a
ports.capacity: Deep-water bulk port built south of Safi for coal (Safi thermal plant) and OCP phosphate/fertiliser exports from the Safi industrial platform
ports.throughput: n/a; first phosphate cargo handled by OCP at the new port (2024-25)
ports.projects: ANP study on optimising roles of old and new Safi ports (2025); OCP Safi industrial platform expansion
ports.notes: Complements Jorf Lasfar as OCP's second Atlantic export outlet. Old Safi port remains for fishing/general cargo (Marsa Maroc).

ports.name: Dakhla Atlantique
ports.operator: Ministry of Equipment and Water / ANP (developer); terminal operators not yet awarded (Marsa Maroc has signalled interest)
ports.concession: n/a (terminal concessions not yet tendered as of 2026)
ports.capacity: Deepest Moroccan port at -23 m; ~2.2m t/year initially (long-run figure of 35m t cited); 950,000 t/year seafood; 1,650 ha industrial-logistics zone; 1,600 ha industrial and 5,200 ha desalinated-irrigation farmland planned
ports.projects: MAD 12-15bn (US$1.3-1.6bn) build; 60% complete Jan 2026, ~62-65% mid-2026; linked El Argoub logistics zone (AMDL studies tendered Sept 2026) and Guerguerat trade zone; green hydrogen, shipbuilding and fish-processing components; part of the Royal Atlantic Initiative to give Sahel states Atlantic access
ports.notes: Positioned to compete with Abidjan, Lomé, Lekki and Ndayane for Sahel cargo via the Guerguerat–Nouadhibou road corridor. Located in Western Sahara: political-risk and legal context to be assessed.

ports.name: Kenitra Atlantique (new port)
ports.operator: Ministry of Equipment and Water / ANP (planned)
ports.capacity: n/a (planned deep-water port to serve the Kenitra–Rabat industrial corridor and relieve Casablanca)
ports.projects: Studied with JICA support (environmental category B); listed in the national port strategy 2030; no construction start confirmed as of 2026
ports.notes: Would serve Atlantic Free Zone (Stellantis cluster) exports currently routed via Tanger Med and Casablanca. Existing Kenitra river port is minor.

zones.name: Tanger Free Zone
zones.incentives: Free-zone customs regime (duty/VAT exemption on inputs), reduced corporate tax under Moroccan industrial-acceleration-zone status, one-stop shop
zones.tenants: Part of the Tanger Med industrial platform: >1,500 companies, ~145,000 jobs, MAD 188bn (US$18.8bn) business volume (2025)
zones.projects: 84 new industrial projects approved across Tanger Med Zones in 2025 (MAD 4.9bn, 11,776 jobs); further extensions
zones.notes: Adjacent to Tangier Ibn Battouta airport; ~45 km from Tanger Med port.

zones.name: Tanger Automotive City
zones.incentives: Free-zone customs and tax regime (industrial acceleration zone)
zones.tenants: Tier 1-3 automotive suppliers to Renault Tanger Med (300 ha plant, 400,000 vehicles/year capacity) and Stellantis Kenitra
zones.projects: Automotive exports from the Tanger Med platform reached MAD 125bn in 2025 (+6.8%)
zones.notes: Located between Tanger Med port and Renault plant on the Tanger Med–Tangier motorway.

zones.name: Medhub (Tanger Med logistics free zone)
zones.incentives: Bonded customs zone adjacent to the port; free-zone fiscal regime; value-added logistics (kitting, labelling, QC) for re-export
zones.tenants: 9 of the world's top-25 3PLs incl. DHL, DB Schenker, Dachser, Nippon Express; industrial distributors
zones.projects: Logistics business volume of the Tanger Med platform MAD 50.4bn in 2025 (+9.6%)
zones.notes: Direct competitor benchmark for DP World's Jebel Ali Free Zone model in the western Med.

zones.name: Atlantic Free Zone Kenitra
zones.area: 600 ha total, of which 350 ha free zone; phase 1 2012, phase 2 2018 (60% occupied); 100 ha extension under negotiation
zones.incentives: Free-zone tax and customs measures; on-site 3.5 GWh solar farm; one-stop shop
zones.tenants: Stellantis Kenitra plant nearby; Coficab, Dicastal, Fujikura, Hirschmann, Nexteer, Saint-Gobain, Simoldes, AGC, Tuyauto; 36,000 jobs
zones.notes: 12 km from Kenitra, 48 km from Rabat, 134 km from Casablanca; on A1 motorway and ONCF main line.

zones.name: Midparc (Nouaceur aerospace free zone)
zones.incentives: Free-zone regime adjacent to Mohammed V airport; export-oriented fiscal incentives
zones.tenants: Safran engine complex, Pratt & Whitney (MAD 715m plant), Aciturri, Spirit/Bombardier heritage site; Safran new engine plant announced 2025-26
zones.projects: Safran expansion (new engine plant at MEDZ park near Casablanca)
zones.notes: Core of Morocco's aerospace cluster; air-cargo oriented rather than port-linked.

zones.name: Haliopolis / Agropole Souss-Massa (Agadir)
zones.area: n/a (Haliopolis + Agropole; third tranche of Agropole launched)
zones.incentives: Industrial-park pricing, CRI one-stop shop annex on site; Zone Franche Souss-Massa free-zone regime within the complex
zones.tenants: Seafood and agri-food processors; number n/a
zones.projects: Third tranche of Agropole Souss-Massa launched; Al Omrane phase III of the Agadir integrated industrial park; new Lqliaa industrial zone approved
zones.notes: Feeds reefer exports through the Port of Agadir.

zones.name: Oujda Technopole
zones.incentives: Free-zone regime in the 40 ha zone; MED-EST regional industrial plan support
zones.tenants: Aptiv (ex-Delphi), Atlas Paints, Auto Hall, Imperial Tobacco, Synergy Cables, Europerfil; ~3,500 jobs
zones.notes: Oriental region hub near the closed Algerian border; future hinterland to Nador West Med via the Oujda–Nador road/rail links.

zones.name: Dakhla Atlantique industrial zone / El Argoub logistics zone
zones.authority: Ministry of Equipment and Water (port zone); AMDL (El Argoub logistics zone); Guerguerat trade zone
zones.area: 1,650 ha port industrial-logistics zone; El Argoub zone size n/a
zones.incentives: n/a (expected to align with southern-provinces investment incentives)
zones.projects: AMDL launched technical studies for El Argoub zone (tender Sept 2026); integrated port–zone–Guerguerat corridor aimed at Sahel markets
zones.notes: Located in Western Sahara; assess legal/political-risk context.

zones.name: Mohammed VI Tanger Tech City
zones.authority: Tanger Med Group / BMCE Bank of Africa / CCCC (China Communications Construction)
zones.incentives: Free-zone regime under Tanger Med Zones
zones.tenants: 11 projects approved in 2025 worth MAD 12.22bn (US$1.22bn), 3,882 jobs
zones.projects: Chinese-partnered industrial city; first phases marketed 2023-2026
zones.notes: Part of the Tanger Med industrial platform statistics.

corridors.name: Tanger Med – Kenitra – Casablanca rail freight corridor
corridors.route: Tanger Med port → Tangier → Kenitra (Atlantic Free Zone) → Rabat → Casablanca / Jorf Lasfar → Marrakech
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: ONCF general freight 9m t (2025, +6%, driven by containers and energy products); phosphate 14.2m t (2025); Renault Tanger Med freight rail shuttle operational
corridors.projects: MAD 96bn national rail programme launched April 2025; Kenitra–Marrakech LGV (430 km, 350 km/h, opening ~2029) will free conventional-line capacity for freight; 168 new trainsets ordered
corridors.notes: Backbone of the Moroccan automotive export chain; road (TIR) still dominant with 535,203 trucks via Tanger Med in 2025.

corridors.name: Nador West Med hinterland corridor (Selouane rail link + Guercif–Nador motorway)
corridors.route: Nador West Med port → Selouane → Taourirt (ONCF main line) / Guercif (A2 motorway) → Fès–Casablanca
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Single-track 160 km/h rail line with marshalling yard at the port; n/a traffic
corridors.projects: Selouane–NWM rail: three road bridges, two rail bridges, port marshalling yard; delivery slipped from end-2024 to 2027; Guercif–Nador motorway MAD 5.5bn, Driouch–NWM section ~80% built, completion 2028
corridors.notes: Critical path for NWM's gateway (non-transhipment) volumes into the Oriental and Fès–Meknès regions.

corridors.name: Atlantic road corridor Tangier – Agadir – Laayoune – Dakhla – Guerguerat (Morocco–Mauritania–Sahel)
corridors.route: Tanger Med / Casablanca → Agadir (A7) → Tiznit–Dakhla expressway (N1) → Guerguerat → Nouadhibou → Nouakchott → Mali/Senegal
corridors.operator: Ministry of Equipment and Water / Autoroutes du Maroc (1,800 km motorway network)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: n/a (main land route for Moroccan fresh-produce exports to Mauritania and West Africa)
corridors.projects: Royal Atlantic Initiative for Sahel access (2023-); Dakhla Atlantique port (2028-29) and El Argoub logistics zone; new Amgala–Bir Moghrein crossing (2025); Tiznit–Dakhla expressway completed
corridors.notes: Only open land border to sub-Saharan Africa; passes through Western Sahara (buffer strip at Guerguerat, 2020 incident).

corridors.name: Nigeria–Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline (African Atlantic Gas Pipeline)
corridors.route: Nigeria → Benin → Togo → Ghana → Côte d'Ivoire → Liberia → Sierra Leone → Guinea → Guinea-Bissau → Gambia → Senegal → Mauritania → Morocco (→ Europe via Maghreb-Europe pipeline)
corridors.projects: Estimated cost ~US$25bn; preliminary technical studies completed; intergovernmental agreement targeted Q4 2026; Nigeria and Morocco seeking US financing (2026)
corridors.notes: Would land on the Moroccan Atlantic coast (Dakhla/Nador West Med LNG links discussed); long-dated, FID not taken.

corridors.name: Casablanca metropolitan motorway upgrades (Continental Rabat–Casablanca, Tit Mellil–Berrechid)
corridors.route: Rabat → Casablanca (Continental highway, 60 km) ; Tit Mellil → Berrechid (30 km) linking Casablanca bypass to A7 Marrakech and Béni Mellal routes
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Relieves the Casablanca–Rabat A1, the country's busiest motorway; n/a AADT
corridors.projects: Continental highway MAD 6.5bn (under construction, 2030 World Cup horizon); Tit Mellil–Berrechid MAD 2.5bn opened 27 Nov 2025; ADM ~MAD 8bn investment to 2027; Fès–Marrakech motorway (420 km, MAD 28bn) in study
corridors.notes: Improves truck access to Casablanca port and Jorf Lasfar from the northern corridor.

corridors.name: Kenitra – Casablanca – Marrakech high-speed rail line (LGV extension)
corridors.route: Kenitra → Rabat → Casablanca (Mohammed V airport) → Marrakech
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: Passenger line (350 km/h); indirect freight benefit by releasing capacity on the conventional Kenitra–Casablanca–Marrakech line
corridors.projects: Civil works launched April 2025 (GCF among contractors); opening targeted 2029 within the MAD 96bn rail programme
corridors.notes: Extends the Tangier–Kenitra Al Boraq line (5.6m passengers in 2025).

border_crossings.name: Bab Sebta / Tarajal (Ceuta)
border_crossings.traffic: Mainly passengers and cross-border workers; commercial customs opened for the first time in January 2025 with limited, pre-agreed goods flows
border_crossings.projects: Commercial customs office opened 16 Jan 2025 (first truck); Spanish 'smart border' technology being deployed (2025); Fnideq economic activity zone developed by Tanger Med Zones to replace informal trade
border_crossings.notes: Historically a hub of informal 'atypical' trade (estimated MAD 4bn/year customs shortfall) shut down by Morocco in 2019-2020; early 2025 crossings hampered by documentation problems.

border_crossings.name: Beni Ensar (Melilla)
border_crossings.traffic: Passengers; commercial customs closed 2018-2025, reopened 15 Jan 2025 with first ~600 kg consignment
border_crossings.projects: Reopening of commercial customs (Jan 2025) under Spain–Morocco 2022 roadmap; smart-border inspection (2025)
border_crossings.notes: Adjacent to Beni Ensar port (Marsa Maroc) and ~30 km from Nador West Med; 2022 Melilla fence incident underlines security sensitivity.

border_crossings.name: Guerguerat (El Guerguerat)
border_crossings.traffic: Main and until 2025 sole land trade gateway from Morocco to Mauritania and West Africa (fresh produce, consumer goods); truck counts n/a
border_crossings.projects: Planned El Guerguerat trade and distribution zone linked to Dakhla Atlantique port; desalination plant (2023) and services added
border_crossings.notes: Crossing passes a UN-monitored buffer strip; Morocco's Nov 2020 operation reopened the road after a Polisario blockade. Located in Western Sahara.

border_crossings.name: Amgala – Bir Moghrein
border_crossings.traffic: n/a (new inland crossing intended to divert Sahel-bound traffic from Guerguerat)
border_crossings.projects: 93 km Smara–Amgala–Tifariti road (MAD 49.7m, >95% complete Feb 2025); 3,600 m2 roadside station; Mauritania designated Bir Moghrein/Aïn Ben Tili crossings by decree (Feb 2025); inaugurated Sept 2025
border_crossings.notes: Second Morocco–Mauritania crossing; lies in Western Sahara near the berm.

border_crossings.name: Zouj Beghal – Akid Lotfi
border_crossings.traffic: None; the 1,559 km land border has been closed since 1994
border_crossings.notes: Opened only exceptionally for repatriations of bodies and returned migrants (2024-2026). Morocco–Algeria trade must move by sea or air; reopening would transform Oujda Technopole and Nador West Med hinterlands.
